Great Expectations. Serialized from 1860 to 1861, this novel follows Pip, an orphan in the Kent marshes, as he moves from country boy to gentleman to a man disillusioned by his own desires. The novel is narrated by the adult Pip, reflecting on a life transformed by ambition and shame. As a boy, Pip helps an escaped convict named Magwitch and is then summoned to Satis House, the home of the wealthy Miss Havisham, to keep company with her adopted daughter Estella. Miss Havisham is a woman frozen in time by heartbreak, jilted on her wedding day decades ago. She has kept Satis House exactly as it was on that day, down to the molding wedding cake. She deliberately uses Estella to make Pip fall in love with her as a form of revenge against men. Estella is beautiful, cold, and emotionally unavailable, the perfect object for Pip's romantic obsession and his greatest source of pain. Pip becomes certain that Miss Havisham is his mysterious benefactor, that she's been grooming him to be worthy of Estella and wealth. But his great expectations are shattered when he discovers the truth: his benefactor is not Miss Havisham at all, but Magwitch, the convict he helped as a boy. This revelation destroys Pip's snobbish ambitions. He has a loyal friend in Herbert Pocket, who serves as his moral anchor throughout. The novel ends ambiguously when Pip encounters Estella again, suggesting the possibility of reunion, though Dickens leaves the question deliberately unresolved.
